faqs.question: How does Spain’s new post-study visa work?
faqs.answer: Under Spain’s current regulations, eligible international graduates can apply for a **24-month, non-renewable residence authorization** to seek suitable employment related to their completed studies or to develop a business project. Applicants must meet the eligibility requirements and submit their application within the applicable deadline. This authorization does not itself permit employment. Once a qualifying job or business opportunity is secured, the graduate must apply for the appropriate residence and work authorization.

faqs.question: Is public tuition the same for Bangladeshi students in Spain?
faqs.answer: It varies by region — some charge non-EU students the EU rate, others charge more. We verify the regional rules for each chosen university before application.

faqs.question: Does Spain offer post-study work rights?
faqs.answer: Yes — the 2024 reform grants a 24-month job-search residence (estancia por búsqueda de empleo), among the most generous in the EU, applied for from inside Spain before the student permit expires.

faqs.question: Is Spain affordable for Bangladeshi students?
faqs.answer: Yes — public master's tuition is €1,500–4,000/year with €560–850/month living outside Madrid and Barcelona. It is one of the best value propositions in the EU with a generous post-study runway.

faqs.question: Do I need to speak Spanish to work in Spain?
faqs.answer: For most local employment outside multinationals and tourism, yes — B1–B2 is effectively required. Start Spanish before departure; it decides whether the 24-month window produces a job.

faqs.question: What causes Spanish visa refusals?
faqs.answer: Insurance and apostille errors more than academic weakness. Choose insurance that explicitly states no co-payment, and apostille the police clearance and academic documents early

faqs.question: What is the cita previa and why does it matter?
faqs.answer: The appointment system for the TIE (foreigner identity card) and other procedures. Appointments fill in hours, so book the moment they open — delays affect enrolment and bank account opening.

faqs.question: Can I get permanent residency in Spain?
faqs.answer: Yes — permanent residence (larga duración) is available after five years of continuous legal residence. Citizenship takes 10 years for (2 years for Ibero-Americans, not applicable).

completeBrief: Spain became a serious post-study destination in 2024, when the new job-search residence gave graduates 24 months to find qualifying employment — matching the UK at a fraction of the tuition. Public universities charge €1,500–4,000 per year, private business schools such as IE and ESADE compete globally, and living costs outside Madrid and Barcelona are moderate.

Spanish at B1–B2 is the practical requirement for local employment outside multinationals and tourism. Students who plan for this from the first semester convert the 24-month window into a job; those who do not often leave when it expires.

Spain's strengths are renewable energy, tourism management, biotech, design and business. The country is a European leader in solar and wind, and the tourism and hospitality management programmes are among the world's best. The 2024 reform also simplified the transition from student to employee status.

For partners, Spain is a value destination with a generous post-study runway, but insurance and apostille errors cause more refusals than academic weakness. Present the 2024 job-search residence explicitly — many families still assume Spain has no post-study route.

faqs.question: Is French language mandatory to study in France?
faqs.answer: Many master’s programmes are English-taught, but French B2 is required for French-taught tracks and strongly improves internships and employment. We recommend starting French alongside the application.

faqs.question: How much does it really cost to study in France?
faqs.answer: Public-route students pay €170–3,770/year tuition plus €700–1,200/month living, with CAF housing aid available in Paris. Private business schools charge €9,000–46,000, so route choice drives the budget.

faqs.question: What is Campus France and why does it matter?
faqs.answer: Campus France runs the mandatory pre-consular interview for Bangladeshi students. A coherent, well-rehearsed study plan is decisive — we prepare every candidate for this interview.

faqs.question: Is France affordable compared to the UK?
faqs.answer: On the public route, yes — master's tuition is €2,902–3,950/year versus £14,000–32,000 in the UK. CAF housing aid further reduces rent by €100–250/month. Private grandes écoles are comparable to UK pricing, so route choice is decisive.

faqs.question: Do I need to speak French to study in France?
faqs.answer: Not for English-taught programmes (over 1,700 exist). But French at B1–B2 is effectively required for internships, most local hiring and permanent residence. Begin French before departure.

faqs.question: What is CAF and am I eligible?
faqs.answer: CAF (Caisse d'Allocations Familiales) is a housing allowance reducing rent by €100–250/month for eligible students. Apply within the first month of arrival; VISALE provides a free state guarantor for under-30s.

faqs.question: Can I stay and work after graduation?
faqs.answer: Yes — master's graduates get a 12-month APS job-search residence. On securing a job at ≥1.5× SMIC, you transition to an employee residence permit. Permanent residence is available after 5 years.

faqs.question: What is the Campus France interview?
faqs.answer: A motivation interview covering programme fit, funding and career plan. It is a genuine gate, not a formality — prepare for it as rigorously as for a visa interview.

completeBrief: France offers the second-lowest public tuition in Western Europe — €243 per year for a master's at a public university — alongside a research base in mathematics, physics, aerospace and luxury management that few countries match. The English-taught catalogue has grown quickly, and Campus France gives Indian applicants a structured, predictable route into the system.

The critical decision is public versus private. A public-route student may complete a master's for under €25,000 in total; a grande école or business school route can cost €25,000–46,000 in tuition alone. Both are legitimate, but they serve different families and different career outcomes, and conflating them in a shortlist damages trust.

France's 12-month APS (Autorisation Provisoire de Séjour) job-search residence for master's graduates, combined with CAF housing aid that reduces rent by €100–250 per month, makes the public route one of the best net-cost propositions in Europe. The 2024 reforms also simplified the transition from student to employee status for graduates who secure a qualifying offer.

For partners, France rewards disciplined route selection. Separate the public-university pipeline from the grande école/business-school pipeline at the first counselling session, because the budgets, deadlines, interview preparation and family conversations are entirely different. Mixing them is the most common cause of mid-cycle walk-aways.

faqs.question: Is there a blocked account for Ireland?
faqs.answer: No. Ireland requires proof of funds rather than a blocked account, plus private medical insurance. This makes the financial setup simpler than Germany’s.

faqs.question: Is accommodation really that hard in Dublin?
faqs.answer: Dublin student housing is scarce and expensive — we set realistic expectations early and help arrange confirmed accommodation before travel where possible.

faqs.question: How long can I work after graduating in Ireland?
faqs.answer: Eligible graduates may qualify for 12 months of post-study permission at Level 8 or up to 24 months at Level 9 or higher, subject to the Third Level Graduate Scheme conditions.

faqs.question: Is Ireland cheaper than the UK?
faqs.answer: Tuition is comparable (€10,000–25,000 vs £14,000–32,000),but costs vary by city and programme. Ireland is an EU member but is not part of the Schengen Area, and student dependants are generally not permitted under the standard student permission. Dublin living costs rival London, so consider Cork, Galway or Limerick for better value.

faqs.question: What is the Critical Skills Employment Permit?
faqs.answer: The Critical Skills Employment Permit is available for eligible occupations and qualifying job offers that meet the applicable salary and permit conditions. It does not require a labour-market needs test. Eligible permit holders may qualify for Stamp 4 permission after 21 months of qualifying employment.

faqs.question: Do I need to show proof of funds for the visa?
faqs.answer: Yes — €10,000 per year of study plus tuition, held in accessible funds. The source of funds is scrutinised, so keep a clean 3–6 month trail before applying.

faqs.question: Can my spouse join me in Ireland?
faqs.answer: Yes — Critical Skills permit holders can bring dependants with work rights. On the student visa, dependants are generally not permitted, so plan the family timeline around the post-study permit.

faqs.question: Are there January intakes in Ireland?
faqs.answer: Yes — many universities offer a January intake with a limited programme set. It is a genuine second chance for students who miss the September deadlines.

completeBrief: Ireland is the clearest English-language alternative inside the European Union. It hosts the European headquarters of Google, Meta, Apple, Intel, Pfizer and a dense pharmaceutical cluster, and its Third Level Graduate Scheme gives master's graduates 24 months to find work without sponsorship. For students who want a UK-style education while staying inside the EU, Ireland is usually the strongest fit.

The constraint is cost, particularly housing. Dublin rents are among the highest in Europe and supply is genuinely tight, so accommodation must be secured before departure rather than on arrival. Universities outside Dublin — Cork, Galway, Limerick — offer materially better value with comparable programme quality and strong regional employer links.

Ireland's Critical Skills Employment Permit is the fastest work-permit route for graduates in shortage occupations (IT, engineering, healthcare, finance), and it does not require a labour-market test. Eligible Critical Skills Employment Permit holders may qualify for Stamp 4 permission after 21 months of qualifying employment. Long-term residence and citizenship follow separate eligibility rules.

For partners, Ireland converts best when financial documentation is impeccable and accommodation is treated as a pipeline stage rather than an afterthought. Refusals here trace to funds-source questions more often than academic weakness, so verify the source of funds before the visa file is built.
